## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (4000–4M) sit above the L1d spill at N≈963, so that transition is invisible. At q=0.01 the curve is essentially FLAT from N=4000 (8.85 ns/p) through N=262000 (8.146 ns/p), with slight improvement reflecting overhead amortization at small N. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 produces no knee — cost actually continues to improve to 8.197 ns/p at N=65000 and 8.146 at N=262000. Only at N≥1000000 does cost RISE gently (8.661, then 8.758 at N=4M), suggesting mild DRAM pressure but no bandwidth wall. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.25 the mid-range floor sits at ~11.2 ns/p versus ~8.1 at q=0.01, with the same flat-then-gentle-rise profile.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.35 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 33% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.25 the peak falls to 6.1 GB/s (24% of ceiling). The algo is overhead- and compute-bound, never bandwidth-bound: it never transitions toward the streaming ceiling at any N or death rate. Higher death rate depresses throughput uniformly (q=0.05 peaks at 7.91 GB/s; q=0.25 at 6.1 GB/s), consistent with branchy respawn cost rather than memory pressure.

## Assembly
The compiler did vectorize, but across the components of a single particle, not across particles. `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` repacks four float components into one register; `fmul.4s v6, v17, v3` and `fadd.4s v6, v7, v6` operate on those four lanes. `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x10]` is an indexed single-element load — a one-component gather — and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]` inserts a lane. The loop advances by 0x44 (68 bytes) per iteration, confirming one particle per trip. Only 9 of 295 instructions are vector-suffixed. The deposit/scatter phase is entirely scalar: 19 `strb`, 12 `ldrb`, 18 `csel`, 9 `fcmp` — byte-granular reads, clamping, and writes that cannot stream. This within-particle vectorization and byte-level scatter explain why bandwidth stalls at 33% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo sustains only 8.35 GB/s = 33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, despite the compiler emitting `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s`/`ext.16b` vectorization. The within-particle vector lanes and the 19 `strb` byte-scatter stores in the deposit phase prevent streaming, and death rate merely raises the floor from 8.1 to 11.2 ns/p without changing the N-shape, confirming the bottleneck is compute and scatter overhead rather than bandwidth.
